guard: a real authenticated agent endpoint creates and deletes only its lifecycle-pinned public-KV watchers, while a same-principal peer lifecycle remains broker-denied
command: corepack pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/core build && PATH=/workspace/state/tools/nats-server-v2.12.12-b:$PATH corepack pnpm smoke:manager-split && PATH=/workspace/state/tools/nats-server-v2.12.12-b:$PATH corepack pnpm smoke:agent-watch-cleanup:auth
why: The stock ordered KV watch generates oc_* names that cannot be authorized per principal. The
agent endpoint instead binds stable lifecycle-owned consumers and its JWT names those exact
CREATE/INFO/DELETE subjects. The real endpoint smoke proves the production branch and cleanup;
the broker matrix proves a same-principal peer lifecycle and generated oc_* names stay denied.
